```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,

  fig.height = 5,
  out.width = "100%"

library(PaleoClimR)
```

## Introduction

PaleoClimR reads cGENIE NetCDF output, prepares gridded data for model
analysis, and creates maps and transect plots. It also includes helpers for
matching palaeogeographic points, identifying shelf cells, summarizing oxygen
conditions, and reading cGENIE `.res` time series.

The package includes a small cGENIE experiment for examples. The functions
expect the path to the experiment directory; the NetCDF files are in its
`biogem` subdirectory, as would be produced by the model itself.

```{r example-path}
cGENIE_exp_path <- PaleoClimR.example("cGENIE.permian.example")
cGENIE_exp_path
```

## Inspecting the grid and NetCDF data

`cGENIE.grid()` returns the horizontal grid coordinates and cell edges. For a
3D field it also returns depth levels and depth edges.

```{r grid}
cgenie_grid <- cGENIE.grid(
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  dims = 3
)

c(
  longitude_cells = length(cgenie_grid$lon),
  latitude_cells = length(cgenie_grid$lat),
  depth_levels = length(cgenie_grid$depth)
)
```

`cGENIE.get.nc()` reads a named field and its coordinates into a list. The
field remains an array, with longitude, latitude, depth, and time dimensions.

```{r get-netcdf}
o2_array <- cGENIE.get.nc(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  dims = 3
)

dim(o2_array$var)
```

`cGENIE.years()` reads the saved time values from the experiment:

```{r years}
cGENIE.years(experiment = cGENIE_exp_path)
```

## Extracting 2D and 3D fields

Use `cGENIE.data()` to extract one horizontal slice. For a 3D field, choose a
depth level. The result includes cell bounds and a `var` column that can be
used by mapping and point-matching functions.

```{r data-2d}
oxygen_surface <- cGENIE.data(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  depth.level = 2
)

head(oxygen_surface)
```

Use `cGENIE.data.3D()` to return the field across all depth levels, with depth
midpoints and bounds attached to each cell:

```{r data-3d}
oxygen_3d <- cGENIE.data.3D(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path
)

head(oxygen_3d)
```

The 2D cGENIE file also contains bottom-water variables. Pass `dims = 2` for
these horizontally gridded fields:

```{r bottom-water-data}
bottom_oxygen <- cGENIE.data(
  var = "ocn_ben_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  dims = 2
)

head(bottom_oxygen)
```

## Mapping cGENIE fields

`cGENIE.map()` creates a map for a selected variable and depth level. The
function applies defaults for common variables, including oxygen scaling and
colour-bar labels.

```{r map-oxygen}
cGENIE.map(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  depth.level = 2
)
```

## Creating transect plots

`cGENIE.transect()` extracts the nearest latitude or longitude band and plots
the selected field against depth. Here, `orientation = "lon"` selects the
latitude band nearest 0° and plots a longitude–depth section.

```{r transect}
cGENIE.transect(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  degrees = 0,
  orientation = "lon",
  continents.outlined = TRUE,
  unit.factor = 1e6,
  min.value = 0,
  max.value = 300,
  scale.label = "Oxygen (µmol/kg)"
)
```

## Identifying shelf cells

`cGENIE.adjacent.land()` marks ocean cells next to cells with `NA` values in a
single horizontal slice. At depth level 2, these missing cells include land
and locations where the seafloor is shallower than that depth.

```{r adjacent-land}
adjacent_oxygen <- cGENIE.adjacent.land(oxygen_surface)
table(adjacent_oxygen$adj.land)
```

`cGENIE.shelf.data()` applies this neighbour check to model output and returns
the cells adjacent to land or missing ocean cells. Set `keep.nas = FALSE` to
return only cells with data.

```{r shelf-data}
shelf_oxygen <- cGENIE.shelf.data(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  depth.level = 2,
  keep.nas = FALSE
)

head(shelf_oxygen[, c("lon.mid", "lat.mid", "var", "adj.land")])
```

`cGENIE.shelf.map()` maps the same shelf subset:

```{r shelf-map}
cGENIE.shelf.map(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  depth.level = 2
)
```

## Matching palaeogeographic points

The bundled occurrence data include palaeogeographic coordinates in `p_lng`
and `p_lat`. `cGENIE.points.data()` assigns each occurrence a model value. By
default, points falling on land or outside the valid model field are matched
to a nearby valid cell within `max_dist` kilometres.

```{r points-data}
data("PBDB.permian.example", package = "PaleoClimR")

matched_occurrences <- cGENIE.points.data(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  depth.level = 2,
  coord.dat = PBDB.permian.example
)

head(matched_occurrences[, c(
  "p_lng", "p_lat", "matched_climate", "lat.bin.mid", "lon.bin.mid"
)])
```

`cGENIE.points.map()` overlays the matched points on the climate map. The
following example colours points by phylum on a separate categorical scale:

```{r points-map}
cGENIE.points.map(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path,
  depth.level = 2,
  coord.dat = PBDB.permian.example,
  points.col = "phylum",
  points.scale.type = "categorical",
  points.scale.label = "Phylum"
)
```

To keep the point scale matched to the map's oxygen scale, omit `points.col`.
The matching options `na.method` and `max_dist` can be changed when calling
either point function.

## Oxygen and redox summaries

`cGENIE.omz()` classifies 3D ocean cells as OMZ or oxygenated using an oxygen
threshold. The default threshold is 58.54 µmol/kg, expressed in the model's
mol/kg units.

```{r omz-cells}
omz_cells <- cGENIE.omz(experiment = cGENIE_exp_path)
head(omz_cells[, c("lon.mid", "lat.mid", "depth", "var", "OMZ.cell")])
```

`cGENIE.omz.thickness()` sums OMZ thickness within each water column, while
`cGENIE.omz.volume()` returns the thickness-weighted proportion of ocean
volume classified as OMZ.

```{r omz-summary}
omz_thickness <- cGENIE.omz.thickness(experiment = cGENIE_exp_path)
head(omz_thickness[, c("lon.mid", "lat.mid", "ocean.thickness", "omz.thickness", "omz.fraction")])

cGENIE.omz.volume(experiment = cGENIE_exp_path)
```

`cGENIE.omz.map()` maps the OMZ thickness by water column:

```{r omz-map}
cGENIE.omz.map(experiment = cGENIE_exp_path)
```

For bottom-water redox, `cGENIE.bw.redox()` classifies ocean cells as anoxic,
suboxic, or oxic and returns the fraction in each class:

```{r bottom-redox}
cGENIE.bw.redox(experiment = cGENIE_exp_path)
```

## Reading cGENIE `.res` files

Some cGENIE experiments include `.res` files with time-series diagnostics.
`cGENIE.res.import()` reads one into a data frame, and `cGENIE.res.plot()`
creates a time-series plot. This example file contains global oxygen
diagnostics.

```{r res-import}
oxygen_series <- cGENIE.res.import(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path
)

head(oxygen_series)
```

```{r res-plot}
cGENIE.res.plot(
  var = "ocn_O2",
  experiment = cGENIE_exp_path
)
```

## Summary

The main cGENIE workflow is to locate an experiment with
`PaleoClimR.example()` or supply a user experiment path, extract fields with
`cGENIE.data()` or `cGENIE.data.3D()`, and use the cGENIE mapping, transect,
point-matching, shelf, and oxygen-analysis functions for downstream work.
